sentences.text: M/S.United India Insurance Company Ltd vs Mr.Aila
Balachandram And Anr on 20 June, 2023

Author: Lalitha Kanneganti
Bench: Lalitha Kanneganti
 The Honourable Smt. Justice Lalitha Kanneganti
 M.A.C.M.A.No.1971 of 2009
Judgment:

1. Aggrieved by the order and decree dated 13.11.2002 in O.P.No.561 of 2000 passed by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum- District Judge, Adilabad, the Insurance Company has filed the present appeal.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-cum- District Judge, Adilabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Having heard Mr. Srinivasa Rao Vutla, learned counsel for the appellant-Insurance Company and Mr.V.Ravi Kiran Rao, learned counsel for the Respondent- Claimant.
Perused the entire material on record.

3. All together three O.P's ie., O.P.No.560 of 2000, 561 of 200 and 669 of 2000 are filed in respect of the same accident that took place on 25.12.1999 at about 11.45 hours at the outskirts of Dahegaon Shivar, Samundrapur Village, while the claimant in all the O.P. and their family members were proceeding to Nirmal from nagpur in a Jeep bearing No.AP-1- D-56.
The Tribunal passed common order in all the above O.Ps.

The present appeal is filed against the order and decree in O.P.No.560 of 2000, wherein the petitioner has claimed compensation an amount of Rs.5,00,000/- and Tribunal has granted an amount of Rs.4,72,500/-.

4. The case of the Insurance Company before the Tribunal is that the owner of the vehicle has committed breach of conditions of the policy as he allowed the injured in all the O.P.s to travel as unauthorized passengers and the driver of the jeep had no valid driving licence to drive the jeep.
The LK, J MACMA_1971_2009 Tribunal has observed that as per Ex.A3 driving license the license is valid from 23-02-199 to 22-02-2002.
It is stated that there are about 20 passengers travelling in the vehicle, as such the Insurance Company is not liable to pay any compensation.

5. The Tribunal has dealt with the said issue and held that the evidence on record reveals that the jeep is not overloaded with many number of passengers, but there are only 8 persons were travelling in the jeep.
It is also observed that under Section 147 of the Motor Vehicle Act, the policy was issued covering the risk of every person.

Under the new Act, the Insurance Company has to issue the policy,
which is consistent with Section 147 of the Motor Vehicles Act, but it cannot limit its liability.
There is no doubt that the policy is the comprehensive policy.
Even, if assuming that there are more number of passengers travelling, as per the coverage the Insurance Company has to pay liability as per the policy.
In this case only 3 persons have claimed the compensation by filing claim-petitions.
It M/S.United India Insurance Company Ltd vs Mr.Aila Balachandram And Anr

1 is not the case of the Insurance Company that 20 persons are claiming compensation.

The Tribunal has come to conclusion that because of the rash and negligent driving of the vehicle, the accident has taken place and also basing on the policy, the Insurance Compnay is liable to pay the compensation.
The Insurance Company has failed to adduce any evidence to show that the accident occurred due to the overload of the Jeep.
Hence, this Court finds that there are no reasons to interfere with the findings of the Tribunal.
Accordingly the appeal is dismissed.
No costs.
07. Pending miscellaneous petitions, if any, shall stand closed.
